chunks: And in the narration of al-Sakuni, he said: Ali عليه السلام said:
Regarding a man who made īlāʾ from his wife and performed ẓihār in a single statement, he said: "Upon him is one expiation."

key_terms.آلَى: he made an oath of abstention from marital relations
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: he pronounced ẓihār against his wife

ai.seo_question: If a man combines īlāʾ and ẓihār against his wife in one statement, does he owe one expiation or more?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man who combines īlāʾ and ẓihār in one statement directed toward his wife. Imam Ali عليه السلام rules that only a single kaffarah is due in such a case, indicating the legal treatment of the combined utterance as requiring one expiation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4839 - In the narration of Al-Sakuni, he said that Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) was asked about a man who both swore an oath (ilaʾ) and declared ẓihar (a form of divorce by comparison) against his wife in a single statement.
Imam (as) said: "
He is obligated to offer only one expiation."
